nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-01.title: Pigeonhole principle
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-01.body:
There are $3$ kinds of coins. With $3$ coins Bob might take one penny, one nickel and one dime, all different, so $3$ is not enough. With $4$ coins, two must be of the same kind by the pigeonhole principle (and Bob has enough nickels and dimes for this to be possible). So the minimum is $4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-01.title: Worst case
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-01.body:
The worst case is to draw one coin of each kind first: penny, nickel, dime. The next coin, whatever it is (a nickel or a dime, since the only penny is gone), matches one already taken. So $3+1=4$ coins are needed.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-02.title: Right triangle
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-02.body:
Let the side be $x$. Since $EF$ crosses the square, $E$ lies beyond $B$ on line $AB$ and $F$ beyond $D$ on line $CD$, on opposite ends. Let $G$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $F$ to line $AB$; then $FG=x$ and $GA=FD=5$, so $GE=5+x+5=x+10$. By Pythagoras,
$$x^2+(x+10)^2=500\implies x^2+10x-200=0\implies(x-10)(x+20)=0.$$
So $x=10$ and the area is $100$.

**Answer: 100**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-02.title: Coordinates
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-02.body:
Let $A=(0,0)$, $B=(x,0)$, $C=(x,x)$, $D=(0,x)$. Then $E=(x+5,0)$ and $F=(-5,x)$, so $EF^2=(x+10)^2+x^2=500$. The positive solution is $x=10$, giving area $100$.

**Answer: 100**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-04.title: Solve for ab
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-04.body:
From the first equation $ab+1=6b$ and from the second $ab+1=4a$, so with $t=ab$: $a=\frac{t+1}4$, $b=\frac{t+1}6$, and $t=ab=\frac{(t+1)^2}{24}$. Thus $t^2-22t+1=0$, and dividing by $t$: $t+\frac1t=22$.

**Answer: 22**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-06.title: Casework on the number of odd digits
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-06.body:
Once we choose which positions hold odd digits and which odd/even digits are used, the order within each parity is forced. The odd digits are distinct, chosen from $5$; the even digits are distinct, chosen from $\{0,2,4,6,8\}$. Because the even digits decrease, $0$ can only be the last even digit, so a leading $0$ is possible only when the number has exactly one even digit and it is in front.
- 4 odd: $\binom54=5$.
- 3 odd, 1 even: $4$ positions for the even digit and $\binom53=10$ odd sets; the even digit has $5$ choices, except $4$ when it is first: $(4+3\cdot5)\cdot10=190$.
- 2 odd, 2 even: $\binom42=6$ position patterns, $\binom52\binom52=100$ digit choices: $600$. (A leading even digit is the larger even one, never $0$.)
- 1 odd, 3 even: $4\cdot5\cdot\binom53=200$.
- 4 even: $\binom54=5$.

Total: $5+190+600+200+5=1000$.

**Answer: 1000**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-06.title: Computer check
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-06.body:
Checking every number from $1000$ to $9999$ for the two monotonicity conditions gives exactly $1000$ valid numbers, matching the casework.

**Answer: 1000**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-07.title: Last digit decides
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-07.body:
Write the number as $10\cdot\overline{abcd}+e$. Since $\overline{abcd}$ is divisible by $3$, so is $10\cdot\overline{abcd}$, and the whole number is divisible by $3$ exactly when $e$ is. Among $1,\dots,9$, the digits $3,6,9$ work: probability $\frac39=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-07.title: Digit sums
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-07.body:
The first four digits have a digit sum divisible by $3$. The full digit sum is divisible by $3$ iff $e\equiv0\pmod3$, true for $3$ of the $9$ equally likely values of $e$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-09.title: Count edges
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-09.body:
An $n$-gonal prism has $n$ edges on each base and $n$ lateral edges: $3n$ edges. So $3n=2019$ gives $n=673$. The faces are the $2$ bases and $673$ lateral parallelograms: $675$.

**Answer: 675**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-09.title: Euler's formula
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-09.body:
The prism has $V=2n$ vertices and $E=3n=2019$ edges, so $n=673$ and $V=1346$. By Euler, $F=2-V+E=2-1346+2019=675$.

**Answer: 675**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-10.title: Pattern
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-10.body:
$9^2=81$, $99^2=9801$, $999^2=998001$: a number of $k$ nines squares to $\underbrace{9\ldots9}_{k-1}8\underbrace{0\ldots0}_{k-1}1$, which has $2k$ digits. For $k=99$: $198$ digits.

**Answer: 198**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-11.title: Sum by length
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-11.body:
There are $4^k$ words of length $k$, for $k=1,\dots,5$: $4+16+64+256+1024=1364$.

**Answer: 1364**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-12.title: Complete a rectangle
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-12.body:
Extend $AE$ past $E$ to $G$ with $EG=FC=4$. Since $AE\perp EF$ and $FC\perp EF$, $FCGE$ is a rectangle, so $GC=EF=5$ and $\angle AGC=90^\circ$. Then $AC=\sqrt{(8+4)^2+5^2}=13$. $AC$ is the diagonal of the square, so $AD=\frac{13}{\sqrt2}=\frac{13\sqrt2}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{13\sqrt2}{2}$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-12.title: Similar triangles
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-12.body:
Let $AC$ meet $EF$ at $H$. Triangles $AEH$ and $CFH$ are similar (right angles at $E,F$, vertical angles at $H$) with ratio $AE:CF=2:1$, so $FH=\frac53$, $HE=\frac{10}3$. Then $CH=\sqrt{16+\frac{25}9}=\frac{13}3$ and $AH=2CH=\frac{26}3$, giving $AC=13$ and $AD=\frac{13}{\sqrt2}=\frac{13\sqrt2}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{13\sqrt2}{2}$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-13.title: Value per pair
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-13.body:
Each dime–quarter pair is worth $35$ cents. With $x$ pairs, the total $35x$ cents must be a multiple of $100$. The least positive $x$ is $20$ (as $\gcd(35,100)=5$, we need $20\mid x$), giving $700$ cents $=\$7$.

**Answer: 7 dollars**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-13.title: LCM
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-13.body:
The total in cents is a common multiple of $35$ and $100$; the least positive one is $\operatorname{lcm}(35,100)=700$ cents, i.e. $7$ dollars (20 dimes and 20 quarters).

**Answer: 7 dollars**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-14.title: Sector minus triangle
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-14.body:
$OA=OB=AB=6$, so $\triangle AOB$ is equilateral and $\angle AOB=60^\circ$. The sector has area $\frac16\cdot\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi$ and the triangle $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot36=9\sqrt3$. The segment's area is $6\pi-9\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $6\pi-9\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-14.title: Segment formula
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-14.body:
The area of a circular segment with central angle $\theta$ is $\frac12r^2(\theta-\sin\theta)$. With $r=6$, $\theta=\frac\pi3$: $18\left(\frac\pi3-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=6\pi-9\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $6\pi-9\sqrt3$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-15.title: Divisible by 4 and 9
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-15.body:
Every permutation has digit sum $45$, so is divisible by $9$. It remains to be divisible by $4$, i.e. its last two digits form a multiple of $4$. Using distinct nonzero digits: $12,16,24,28,32,36,48,52,56,64,68,72,76,84,92,96$, which is $16$ endings. The other $7$ digits can be arranged in $7!$ ways: $16\cdot5040=80640$.

**Answer: 80640**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-15.title: Count endings by last digit
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-15.body:
The last digit must be even. If it is $2$ or $6$, the tens digit must be odd: $5$ choices each. If it is $4$ or $8$, the tens digit must be even (and different): $3$ choices each. That is $2\cdot5+2\cdot3=16$ endings, and $16\cdot7!=80640$.

**Answer: 80640**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-16.title: Circle meets ray
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-16.body:
$D$ lies on a ray from $A$ making $27^\circ$ with $AB$ and on the circle centered at $B$ with radius $BC$. Reflecting across $AB$ does not change $\angle ABD$, so we may take $D$ on ray $AC$. The circle meets this ray at $C$ (giving $\angle ABD=13^\circ$) and at one other point $D$. In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BCA=180^\circ-27^\circ-13^\circ=140^\circ$, so $\angle BCD=40^\circ$. Triangle $BCD$ is isosceles with $BC=BD$, so $\angle BDC=40^\circ$ and $\angle DBC=100^\circ$. Hence $\angle ABD=100^\circ+13^\circ=113^\circ$.

**Answer: $113^\circ$ and $13^\circ$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-16.title: Angle sum check
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-16.body:
In $\triangle ABD$, $\angle BAD=27^\circ$ and $\angle ADB=\angle BDC=40^\circ$, so $\angle ABD=180^\circ-27^\circ-40^\circ=113^\circ$. The other possibility, $D=C$, gives $13^\circ$. These are the only two points of the ray at distance $BC$ from $B$.

**Answer: $113^\circ$ and $13^\circ$**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-17.title: Count by area
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-17.body:
Think of the diagram as a $3\times3$ grid with two segments missing, leaving $5$ unit squares and two $1\times2$ cells. Counting rectangles by area: area 1: $5$; area 2: $6$; area 3: $2$; area 4: $3$; area 6: $2$; area 9: $1$. Total $5+6+2+3+2+1=19$.

**Answer: 19**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-17.title: Choose sides
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-17.body:
In a full $3\times3$ grid there are $\binom42^2=36$ rectangles. Label grid lines $0$–$3$ in each direction; the missing pieces are one unit of interior line $1$ in each direction. A rectangle is lost exactly when one of its sides would run along a missing unit. Checking all $36$ choices of two lines in each direction, $17$ are lost and $19$ rectangles remain.

**Answer: 19**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-18.title: Coprime to 2019
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-18.body:
With $a=2019-b$ and $a,b$ positive, $1\le b\le2018$, and $\gcd(a,b)=\gcd(2019,b)$. So we count $b<2019$ coprime to $2019=3\cdot673$. Multiples of $3$: $672$; of $673$: $2$; none of both. So $2018-672-2=1344$.

**Answer: 1344**

nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-18.title: Euler's totient
nyciml-2019-20-fall-sophfrosh-18.body:
The count is $\varphi(2019)=\varphi(3)\varphi(673)=2\cdot672=1344$, since each $b$ coprime to $2019$ with $1\le b\le2018$ gives a different fraction $\frac{2019-b}{b}$.

**Answer: 1344**
